name: GSG on 42 Ω microstrip: good SIG contact (30 mΩ)

example.note: Two GSG probes on 0.5 in of 42 Ω microstrip, seen from the calibrated tips; the 50 Ω sections stand for the probes. A microstrip, not a stripline: a probe needs the trace on the surface. Its field is partly in air, so Dk is the effective 2.70 of a 42 Ω microstrip on Dk 3.35. Both contacts are 30 mΩ. The lines have some loss (0.2 dB/in at 10 GHz, 0.1 Ω/in at DC), so the TDR creeps up a little: the 42 Ω line reads about 42.7 Ω. Pads and ground vias are left out; add a C chip at the tip to see how a launch pad changes the picture. Store it with Data → Memory before opening the next two.
example.author: TDR Painter
